controls.title: Organizational mission understood and informs cybersecurity risk management
controls.summary: The vendor's cybersecurity risk decisions are informed by a clear understanding of its own organizational mission and stakeholder expectations.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for risk decisions that reference business context, not a generic boilerplate policy.

controls.title: Risk management objectives established and agreed
controls.summary: Risk management objectives are established by organizational leadership and communicated across the vendor's teams.
controls.validationGuidance: Evidence should show leadership sign-off, not just an IT-authored document.

controls.title: Requirements to address cybersecurity risks in supply chains are established
controls.summary: The vendor integrates cybersecurity requirements into its own supplier and partner contracts.
controls.validationGuidance: Check that supply chain requirements flow down contractually, not just informally.

controls.title: Inventories of hardware managed by the organization are maintained
controls.summary: The vendor maintains a current inventory of physical devices and systems within its environment.
controls.validationGuidance: Ask when the inventory was last updated - stale inventories are a common gap.

controls.title: Vulnerabilities in assets are identified and documented
controls.summary: The vendor runs a vulnerability identification process across its systems and documents findings.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for a recurring cadence, not a one-time assessment.

controls.title: Identities and credentials for authorized users are managed
controls.summary: The vendor has a lifecycle process for issuing, managing, and revoking user identities and credentials.
controls.validationGuidance: Confirm timely deprovisioning of access upon termination is part of the process.

controls.title: Access permissions are defined and enforced based on least privilege
controls.summary: Access to systems and data is granted based on need, following least-privilege and separation-of-duties principles.
controls.validationGuidance: Ask for evidence of periodic access reviews, not just initial provisioning controls.

controls.title: Data-at-rest is protected
controls.summary: Sensitive data stored by the vendor is protected using encryption or equivalent controls appropriate to its classification.
controls.validationGuidance: Confirm encryption standards used (e.g. AES-256), not just a claim that 'data is encrypted.'

controls.title: Software is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk
controls.summary: The vendor has a patch management process to keep software current and retire unsupported components.
controls.validationGuidance: Ask for the target patching SLA by severity, not just a stated commitment to patch.

controls.title: Networks and network services are monitored to find potentially adverse events
controls.summary: The vendor continuously monitors its network traffic and services for signs of malicious or anomalous activity.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for a named monitoring tool/SOC function, not a passive log-collection-only setup.

controls.title: Potentially adverse events are analyzed
controls.summary: Detected events are triaged and analyzed to determine whether they represent genuine security incidents.
controls.validationGuidance: Confirm a defined triage SLA exists, not just ad hoc review.

controls.title: The incident response plan is executed once an incident is declared
controls.summary: The vendor has a documented, tested incident response plan that is actually invoked when incidents occur.
controls.validationGuidance: Ask for evidence of the plan being tested or used, not just its existence.

controls.title: Internal and external stakeholders are notified of incidents
controls.summary: The vendor notifies affected customers and relevant stakeholders of security incidents within a defined timeframe.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for a specific notification SLA (e.g. 72 hours), not vague language.

controls.title: The recovery portion of the incident response plan is executed
controls.summary: The vendor has a tested process to restore systems and operations following a disruptive incident.
controls.validationGuidance: Ask for evidence of an actual recovery test or exercise, such as a tabletop or failover drill.

controls.title: Public relations and reputation are managed after a recovery event
controls.summary: The vendor has a plan for managing external communications and reputation following a significant security incident.
controls.validationGuidance: Lower priority for vendors without a public-facing brand relevant to the engagement.
